policy_citations.section: SNF Level of Care - Definitions and Reference Guide › Definitions, Skilled need
policy_citations.quote: Skilled need: A service that requires the involvement of licensed nursing or therapy staff, and could not be safely or effectively provided by non-skilled caregivers.

policy_citations.quote: Non-covered day: A day within an otherwise covered stay where documentation does not support the billed level of care for that specific day; does not require the entire stay to be denied.

policy_citations.section: SNF Level of Care - Definitions and Reference Guide › How to use this guide
policy_citations.quote: Start with the payer-specific guideline in Payer Guidelines that matches the claim's plan. Confirm the guideline's effective date covers the claim's date of service before applying it; if it doesn't, check Archive - DO NOT USE for a version that does.

system_note: Billed line: revenue code 0192 (rehabilitation therapy) for 15 days, 07/01/2026-07/21/2026. Clinical documentation: the facility's therapy record shows dedicated PT and OT sessions on the claimed rehabilitation dates, typically PT = 90 minutes and OT = 60 minutes on each documented therapy date (combined ≈150 minutes/day), indicating active licensed therapy involvement rather than only custodial care. The SNF Level-of-Care reference guide defines the basis for rehabilitation per-diem as services requiring licensed therapy/nursing involvement and maps revenue code 0192 to rehabilitation therapy (see evidence). The guide also defines a Non-covered day as an isolated date where documentation does not support the billed level rather than requiring denial of the entire stay. The facility did not record any explicit per-diem-level exception statements for these dates (level_determination_statement null), and the reference guide and retrieved materials show no payer-specific numeric-minute threshold to require further minute-based reclassification. Taken together, the documented daily skilled therapy (licensed PT and OT) supports the billed 0192 per-diem for the full billed date range. Citations: Policy definitions for Skilled need and Revenue codes justify treating documented licensed therapy involvement as the skilled basis for 0192, and the Non-covered day definition supports per-day assessment rather than whole-claim denial. See evidence entries pol_004-pol_006 below for the exact policy passages relied on. Billed line: revenue code 0191 (skilled nursing) for 5 day(s), DOS range 2026-07-01 through 2026-07-21. The facility's daily clinical notes (get_daily_services) show consistent skilled therapy delivery across the stay (regular PT sessions of 90 minutes and OT sessions of 60 minutes on the dates within the billed range). get_per_diem_level_notes returned no explicit per-date downcoding statements (level_determination_statement is null for every date), which the reference guide explains is common when the billed level's documentation meets requirements and no exception is recorded. There is no payer-specific Aetna Medicare Advantage guideline available in the dataset; we apply the payer-agnostic SNF Level of Care reference guide. Under that reference guide, a "skilled need" is defined as a service requiring licensed nursing or therapy staff and not safely provided by non-skilled caregivers, and revenue code 0191 is the SNF skilled nursing per-diem code. Because: (1) the daily record documents skilled therapy services (PT and OT minutes) on the dates in question, (2) the facility-coded daily per-diem counts (established from the record) show 6 days documented at 0191 (greater than the billed 5), and (3) there are no facility-level notes or policy evidence returned that contradict the presence of skilled need on the billed dates, the documentation supports the billed 5 days at revenue code 0191 as submitted. Therefore no adjustment is required to this revenue line. Evidence relied on: SNF Level of Care reference guide definitions for "skilled need" and the mapping of revenue codes; note that no payer-specific guideline was available in the dataset and get_per_diem_level_notes had no explicit downcoding statements for any date.
